findings.title: 0304's tail verifies ACL preservation for two of the three externally-granted doors it recuts, not all three — list_accrual_adjustments's grant is never re-checked
findings.evidence: The migration recuts ten bodies (measured: the prestate/tail pin tables at lines ~95-127 and ~1316-1339 list _assert_accrual_account, _assert_accrual_particulars, _assert_accrual_world, _accrual_canonical, _accrual_journal_basis, _accrual_finish, correct_accrual_adjustment, get_accrual_adjustment, list_accrual_adjustments, _plan_accrual_period_line). Three of those ten are externally granted doors (grep confirms grants only on correct_accrual_adjustment, get_accrual_adjustment, list_accrual_adjustments — the rest are internal). The tail's '6 · THE DOORS' GRANTS ARE UNMOVED' section (line 1364) explicitly re-checks has_function_privilege for correct_accrual_adjustment (1367), get_accrual_adjustment (1375) and create_accrual_adjustment_for (1381), but list_accrual_adjustments never appears in any has_function_privilege call in this file (grep for 'has_function_privilege' in 0304 returns zero hits mentioning list_accrual_adjustments). The dynamic-SQL corpus entry the same commit adds for this file (apps/web/tests/firm-scope-db-pins.corpus.ts) claims in its own reason string that the tail re-checks 'every door grant it must not have moved' — which overstates what the tail actually verifies.
findings.required_fix: Add a has_function_privilege block for clara.list_accrual_adjustments(uuid,date,date) (clara_authenticated granted, clara_runtime and public not) alongside the other two door checks in the '6 · THE DOORS' GRANTS ARE UNMOVED' section, matching 0303's own pattern for the same two doors. Runtime risk is low (CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION preserves ACL by Postgres's own semantics and no explicit GRANT/REVOKE touches this function in 0304), so this is a self-verification completeness gap against the house law quoted in the review brief ('owner, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path and ACL preserved on recut bodies') and against the migration's own stated intent, not a live security defect.

findings.title: The skip/reverse two-mode local state machine is duplicated verbatim between the two remedy surfaces
findings.evidence: AccrualBillConflictAffordance (needs-you inbox, lines 27-91) and AccrualBillConflictItem inside apps/web/components/accruals/accrual-bill-conflicts.tsx (lines 62-140) both declare `const [skipping, setSkipping] = useState(false)` / `const [reason, setReason] = useState("")`, an identical `reverseNow`/`submitSkip` pair calling the same two api.ts functions with the same argument shape, and near-identical idle/entering-a-reason JSX (Input + two Buttons vs. two Buttons). This is Fowler's Duplicated Code: extract the shared state machine (idle/entering-reason, the two handlers) into one hook (e.g. useAccrualBillConflictRemedies(row, act)) that both components call, leaving only the two render shells distinct.
findings.required_fix: No fix required from this reviewer — self-disclosed by the ticket #938 report's own 'Follow-ups worth filing' section ('A skip reason UX nuance... worth revisiting if a THIRD surface ever needs the same two remedies'), a defensible judgement call to keep two independently-reviewable ~40-line components rather than introduce a shared hook for two call sites. Recorded here per the smell-baseline instruction; not a blocker.
